summary: Daniel B. Stevenson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his Ph.D. from Columbia University. He taught at Butler University (attested 1986) and the University of Kansas (attested 1996–2003), and was a guest scholar at IRIAB.

Daniel Boucher specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Indology, having studied at Indiana University and the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair, Ludo Rocher, and Gregory Schopen. He served as an associate professor at Cornell University (attested 2000–2026).

Daniel Clarke Waugh works in Iranian and Central Asian studies as well as history and archaeology. He studied at Yale University (B.A. 1963) and Harvard University (Master's 1965, 1972), joining the faculty of the University of Washington in 1972.

Daniel Coit Gilman (1831–1908) studied at Yale, Harvard, Cambridge, and Berlin. He served as librarian at Yale (1856–1872), president of UC Berkeley (1872–1875), founding president of Johns Hopkins University (1875–1901), and president of the Carnegie Institution (1902–1904).

Daniel Cozort (born 1953) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later holding positions at Bates College (~1987–1988) and Dickinson College (~1988–2020).

Daniel Dubuisson (born 1950) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held appointments as director of research at the CNRS / National Centre for Scientific Research (~1980–2015) and at Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III (~1989–2015).

Daniel H. H. Ingalls (1916–1999) was an Indologist and philosopher educated at Harvard University under Walter Eugene Clark and W. V. O. Quine, as well as under Kalipada Tarkacharya. He was appointed professor at Harvard University in 1939.

Daniel John Gogerly (1792–1862) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He ran the Wesleyan Mission Press (~1818–1834), chaired the Wesleyan Methodist Missionary Society (1838), and was president of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka (~1856–1858).

Daniel L. Overmyer (1935–2021) specialized in Sinology and religious studies, earning degrees from Westmar, Evangelical Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago under Philip A. Kuhn. He was a professor at the University of British Columbia (~1973–2001).

Daniel M. Neuman (born 1944) works in Indology and ethnomusicology, holding degrees from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and the University of Chicago. He taught at Dartmouth (1971–1980), University of Washington (1980–1995), and UCLA (~1994–2018).

Daniel M. Stuart is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at UC Berkeley under Alexander von Rospatt. He held posts at the University of South Carolina (attested 2017) and the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).
Daniel P. Brown (1948–2022) specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Geshe Wangyal and served as a professor at Harvard University from approximately 1983 to 2021.
Daniel R. Tuzzeo works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his graduate thesis research at Florida State University under the supervision of Jimmy Yu, Bryan J. Cuevas, and Joseph Hellweg.

Daniel Schlumberger (1904–1972) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Strasbourg (~1921–1925) and later held an appointment at Princeton University (~1968–1970).

Daniel Sperber (born 1940) is a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at Kol Torah, Yeshivah of Flatbush, and University College London (~1965–1968). He held academic posts at Bar-Ilan University (~1968–2010) and the Open University of Israel.

Daniel Stuart Capper works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned a BA and MA at the University of Virginia, studying under Robert P. Scharlemann and Jeffrey Hopkins, and completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (attested 2000).

Daniel Timothy Aitken is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Tasmania, having studied under teachers Parimal G. Patil, Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, and Jay L. Garfield.

Daniel Veidlinger specializes in Buddhist and religious studies, completing his PhD at the University of Chicago under Steven Collins (attested 2002). He was a research associate at Chiang Mai University (1999) and held a post at CSU Chico (attested 2006).

Daniel W. Kent is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia. He held instructor positions at both the University of Virginia and Mary Baldwin University (attested 2010).

Daniela Berti is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who earned a PhD in Research Methodology in Ethno-Anthropology from the University of Siena. She was a fellow at Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya (attested 2004).
